role.altitude: The nurse's week is still the bedside, the round and the record. Less of it is retyping monitor rows, paper results and the history. Watching the patient, judging pain and sedation, and the ward round stay at full length.
reach: Physicians: the compiled row and the one-line plan change, the same shift
The next nurse: a history and findings note that was checked sentence by sentence
skills_to_grow: Confirm a monitor row is this patient before trusting it
Reject a drafted sentence that changes what the patient said
Say on the round what changed, not the whole chart
role.ambitious_version: At handover the row, the scores and the note are already on one record. The nurse still watches the patient, still judges sedation, and still speaks the plan with the team.

steps.what: See the monitoring display and the patient at the bedside.
Compile monitoring values from the feed rather than a pad.
Copy diagnostic tests obtained on paper into the chart.
Analyze the compiled row at the bedside before the next hour.

tasks.design: The bedside watch and the analysis stay as they are. The {OTHER} record takes the monitor feed (heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, ventilator settings) and the laboratory message (test name, value, unit, result time). The nurse confirms the row is this patient and types only a gap or a paper result.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same numbers were read on the monitor and written again on the chart.
tasks.enabler_now: A monitor feed and a laboratory message already exist in ordinary ward software.
tasks.still_hard: An unlinked monitor, a paper blood gas, and what the trend means.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse knows whether the feed is this patient and whether a number is an artefact.

ambition.what: Catch a worsening trend the same hour because the row is already compiled.

tasks.altitude: The watch and the analysis stay at full length. The pad is no longer retyped when the feed and the laboratory message arrive.

reach.learn: Which way the numbers moved since the last hour

reach.task: See which results still arrive on paper
reach.learn: Which tests never send a message

evidence.claim: No digest source times how long this nurse spends compiling monitor values or paper diagnostic results. The saving is the retyping this design removes, not a published minute count.
A plot of stored numbers over the hour is plain code. The digest treats calculations of this kind as plain code, and no model sets a treatment from the row.
The compiled row is part of the patient dossier, which is kept twenty years after the last change.
The analysis is not a solely automated care decision. The nurse still judges the row.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is the nurse at the bedside with the monitor and the chart. The prior 54.9 percent in person is that watch, not a meeting. The analysis is also at the bedside, so the in-person steps are 62. Documents are the paper-result copy (22 against a prior 24.1). Screens are the feed confirm (16 against 15.6). The small spreadsheet and mail shares are not a separate pad or inbox.

Monitor contract, produced on this task: the bedside monitor writes heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and ventilator settings during the watch. The nurse confirms the row is this patient. If the feed fails, the nurse copies those fields from the display, and that copy is the remaining 40 percent of the compile step. Monitor runtime is not nurse time.

Laboratory contract, produced on the laboratory task, not this one: test name, value, unit and result time, when the analyser finishes. If the message is missing, the nurse types the paper slip, and that typing is the remaining 40 percent of the copy step. Laboratory capture time is not taken as a saving here.

No second signature. The nurse's confirmation sits inside the compile step. A trend plot does not decide treatment. Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 is the device-field list when a monitor is added, not the per-row confirm and not the outage retype.
unknowns: Which bedside monitors on this unit already write a row into the record, and which tests still arrive only as a paper slip.
research_questions: On a typical shift, what share of diagnostic results still has to be typed from paper?

already_counted.description: Watching the display and the patient, unchanged.
Confirming the feed is this patient and filling a gap when the row is short.
Typing a diagnostic result that the laboratory message did not carry.
Judging what the row means before the next hour, unchanged.

incremental.description: Keeping the list of fields a newly added monitor must send. Not the per-row confirm and not the outage retype.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A shift where the monitor feed and the laboratory message both arrive saves the retyping. A shift of paper blood-gas slips and an unlinked monitor keeps the copying. The watch and the analysis stay full length either way.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess patients' pain at the bedside by asking and by watching.
Judge sedation requirements from how the patient responds.
Read the last pain levels on the open chart.
Write the new pain levels as a number on the chart.

tasks.design: Asking, watching and judging sedation stay at full length. The {OTHER} chart shows the last pain score on the open record, produced when the previous assessment on this task was saved, and the scale is already on the form so the nurse taps the number. A missing score is still paged back, and a missing form is still written as a sentence. No model scores pain or sedation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last score sat pages back, and the new score was written out as a sentence.
tasks.enabler_now: The record already has a structured score field and a scale on the form.
tasks.still_hard: A patient who cannot speak, and deciding what the score means for sedation.
tasks.human_edge: Only the nurse at the bedside sees how the patient responds.

ambition.what: Spot a rising score the same round because the last number is on the open chart.

tasks.altitude: Asking, watching and judging sedation stay at full length. Paging back and writing a sentence are shorter when the last score and the scale are already on the form.

reach.learn: The score the nurse just charted
The last pain number without paging back

evidence.claim: No digest source times a pain or sedation assessment. The saving is paging and the sentence, not the bedside judgement.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner. This assessment does not itself authorise a drug, and a draft is not a prescription.
The sedation requirement is not a solely automated care decision. The nurse judges it at the bedside.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the prior 73 percent in person is the bedside assessment, not a meeting. Asking and judging sedation are those 73 points and stay at full length. Screens are reading the last score (8 against a prior 6.1). Documents are writing the new number (19 against 19.1). The tiny spreadsheet and mail shares are not a separate step.

Last-score contract, produced on this same task: when an assessment is saved it stores score, scale name, time and patient. The next open chart shows that score, so the nurse does not page back. If the field is empty, paging back is the other half of that step.

The form's scale is configuration, not a model. The nurse taps the number. If the form is missing, they write the sentence, and that is the other half of the write step. The nurse does not prescribe; a separate order is another role's task.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 is one later correction of a score filed on the wrong patient, not the entry itself.
unknowns: Which pain scale and which sedation scale this unit uses, and whether a sedation change needs a physician order before the nurse gives it.
research_questions: What share of these assessments are of patients who cannot speak?

already_counted.description: Asking and watching at the bedside, unchanged.
Judging sedation from the patient's response, unchanged.
Paging back when the last score field is empty.
Writing a sentence when the scale is not on the form.

incremental.description: One later correction of a score filed on the wrong patient. Not the entry itself.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A round where the last score is on the open chart saves the paging and the sentence. A patient who cannot speak keeps the bedside assessment at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Treatment plans with the care team

steps.what: Gather identified needs and assessment data from the open sheet.
Collaborate with other health professionals during the round.
Develop and revise treatment plans based on the round.
Write only the change the round just named.

tasks.design: The round stays at full length. Before it, the {OTHER} record shows one sheet: the monitor row from the compile task, the pain and sedation scores from the assessment task, the problem list, and current orders from the prescriber. The nurse adds only the change the round named. A missing line is still typed. No model drafts the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same scores and orders were copied into a handover note before anyone spoke.
tasks.enabler_now: Those fields are already stored by the earlier tasks and by order entry.
tasks.still_hard: A new admission with an empty problem list, and what the team agrees in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse hears what the team actually decided, which a sheet cannot invent.

ambition.what: Revise the plan the same shift when the assessment changes, because the latest scores are already on the sheet.

tasks.altitude: The round stays at full length. The handover note is no longer retyped when the sheet is already filled.

reach.learn: The one-line change, not a recopied chart
The one-line change the round just named

evidence.claim: No digest source times a ward round. The saving is the recopied handover note, not the talking.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative tools, and the inspector names medication errors from wrong registration. This design does not generate the plan.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner. The written change is not a generated prescription.
The plan is not a solely automated care decision. The team agrees it on the round.
The accepted plan stays in the dossier, which is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the prior 61.2 percent in person is the nurse's time in the round, not a separate meeting. Listening and revising the plan are 62 points and stay at full length. Screens are the open sheet (7 against 6.7). Documents plus the small mail share are writing the change (31). There is no separate inbox step. The prior that this is something to generate is declined: the plan is a clinical judgement on the round.

Sheet contract. Fields: problem, latest pain score, latest sedation score, latest vital-sign row, current orders. Producers: the compile task stores the vital-sign row after the nurse confirms it; the pain task stores the scores when that assessment is saved; the prescriber's order entry stores current orders on the prescribing task, not this one. Capture time stays on those producing tasks and is not a saving here. If a field is missing, the nurse types it, and that typing is the remaining part of the gather and of the write.

No separate signature after the round. No model drafts the plan. Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 is one rewrite of a plan line after the round has dispersed, not the writing that remains inside the write step.
unknowns: Whether this unit's nursing care plan is a separate document from the medical orders, and who may change a vasopressor or sedation order.
research_questions: Which plan lines does the nurse write, and which only the intensivist writes?

already_counted.description: Typing a sheet line that the earlier tasks did not store.
Listening and speaking on the round, unchanged.
Revising the plan in the room, unchanged.
Writing the named change, and typing a line the sheet did not already hold.

incremental.description: One rewrite of a plan line after the round has dispersed. Not the writing that remains on the write step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A round where the sheet is already filled saves the re-copy. A new admission with an empty problem list keeps the gather and the write longer. The round itself stays full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear medical histories from patients at the bedside.
Watch assessment findings on the patient during the exam.
Type a monitor number the note left blank.
Document patients' medical histories from the dictated lines.

loop.input: The nurse's dictated lines, the assessment findings just observed, and any number typed for a blank.
loop.output: A draft history and findings note.
loop.check: The nurse rejects a sentence that adds a symptom, a dose, or a finding they did not see or hear.
loop.stop: One draft only. If the nurse rejects it, they type the note themselves.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed form cannot phrase a free-text history.

tasks.design: Hearing the history and watching the exam stay as they are. The {OTHER} record stores a draft made from the nurse's dictated lines, and the nurse rejects any sentence that changes what was said or seen before the note is stored. Monitor numbers already stored are not typed again.
tasks.previous_blocker: The history was heard once and then written out in full, including numbers already on the monitor.
tasks.enabler_now: Ordinary record software can draft from dictated lines, and the clinician still validates before write-back.
tasks.still_hard: A patient who cannot speak, a draft that omits or invents a finding, and the twenty-year record.
tasks.human_edge: Only the nurse knows whether a sentence matches what they heard and saw.

ambition.what: Correct an omitted finding the same shift, while the exam is still fresh, because the draft is waiting.

tasks.altitude: The interview and the exam stay at full length. The writing is shorter and still checked sentence by sentence.

reach.learn: A history and findings note checked sentence by sentence
Findings the nurse accepted, not a sentence the draft invented

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates. It claims 15 to 20 minutes saved per consult, with no method. That figure is not this task's saving, and it is not a measurement of an intensive-care history.

At Capio Ramsay Santé, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes across 236,153 Tandem notes, and median editing stayed 93 seconds. Three of seven authors work for the vendor. This is not a measurement on this ward and not a measurement of the bedside interview.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry a class IIa medical-device mark. This design does not claim that mark.
The draft is validated before storage because providers are responsible for careful generative use, and the inspector names medication errors from wrong registration.
The accepted note is part of the dossier kept twenty years after the last change.
Filing the note is not a solely automated care decision, because the nurse accepts it.
Ambient recording of staff needs works-council consent. This design is nurse-started dictation, not a device that hears the whole bay.
No digest source times this nurse's history-taking. The published note-time drop is a ceiling for the writing step only.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the prior 48.6 percent in person is the interview and the exam. Those two steps are 49 points and stay at full length. Screens are filling a blank monitor number (16 against 17.9). Documents are the history note (35 against 31.1, with the small mail share inside the note). There is no separate inbox.

Dictation is the nurse speaking the lines they just heard and saw. It is not ambient recording of the room. If a later device hears the whole bay, that is a different design and needs works-council consent. This design does not.

Vitals contract, produced on the compile task, not this one: heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and ventilator settings, after the nurse confirms the row. Capture time stays on that task. If the row is absent, the nurse types the numbers, and that typing is the remaining 65 percent of the blank-number step.

The draft reads only the nurse's dictated lines, the observed findings, and stored numbers. It does not invent history. One draft only. The nurse's review is the remaining 78 percent of the document step, already counted, not a second deduction. A data-protection assessment is expected because the loop runs on health data (model knowledge).

Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 is a sample reread for an omitted finding, outside the per-note review. The office note-time case is not this unit. The writing steps together lose less than the published 29 percent note-time drop, and the interview is not cut.
unknowns: Whether this unit already allows nurse-started dictation into the record.
research_questions: How much of this note is free text, and how much is structured scores?

already_counted.description: Hearing the history at the bedside, unchanged.
Typing a monitor number the stored row left blank.
Correcting the draft sentence by sentence, or typing the note if the draft is rejected.

incremental.description: A sample reread of accepted notes for an omitted finding. Not the per-note review already inside the document step.

approvals.approved_version: The draft history and findings note, after the nurse has rejected any sentence that changes what was said or seen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A note the nurse dictates, with monitor numbers already stored, saves part of the writing. A patient who cannot speak, or a draft the nurse rejects, keeps the exam and most of the writing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
